summary: Full end-to-end testing of LIMS backend + frontend. Backend: 33/33 pytest tests passed covering auth (all 3 roles + wrong password + protected /auth/me), role gating (QC/QA cannot list users), seed data (points/params/specs), full sample workflow (create -> results eval PASS/WARN/FAIL -> appearance mismatch FAIL -> QC cannot approve -> QA reject requires comment -> reject creates OOS log -> resubmit + approve -> approved sample locked (400 on further results) -> CoA export), specifications version increment + QC read-only, audit trail (LOGIN/CREATE/ENTER_RESULT/UPDATE_RESULT/SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW/QA_APPROVE/QA_REJECT/EXPORT_COA all present, filter by action + user_email works, UPDATE_RESULT has before/after), user management (min 8 char password, create, role change, deactivate blocks login), dashboard KPIs. Frontend Playwright: login for all 3 roles, wrong password shows friendly error, QC blocked from /qa-review and /users (access-denied testid), QA can access /qa-review but blocked from /users, Admin can access all pages including /users, sample registered with REC-20260811-0003 id, QC does not see qa-approve-btn after submitting, export-coa-btn present, specifications page loads.

issues: Radix DialogContent missing aria-describedby / Description (a11y warning in console)
Recharts responsive container logs width(-1)/height(-1) warning when container has no explicit min height

action_items: (Optional a11y) Add DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to Register-sample and other DialogContent components to silence Radix warning.
(Optional) Give the QA Review / Dashboard chart container an explicit min-height so Recharts stops logging width(-1)/height(-1) warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: next_record_id uses global samples count instead of per-date count - counter never resets per day, so REC-YYYYMMDD-NNNN sequence keeps growing across dates (e.g. today's first sample was REC-20260811-0003). Acceptable if globally unique is the intent, but the -NNNN suffix is misleading as a daily counter.

Login brute-force lockout key includes request.client.host, but behind ingress this is typically the proxy IP - all users share the same lock scope per email. Works but consider using X-Forwarded-For.
CORS: allow_origins hardcodes localhost:3000 as fallback + FRONTEND_URL. CORS_ORIGINS env var declared in .env is not actually consumed by server.py.
cookies use samesite='none'; secure=True which is fine on HTTPS preview, but will fail on local http dev.
server.py is ~680 lines - approaching the 700 line threshold, split routers (auth/samples/specs/users/audit) into modules for maintainability.
@app.on_event('startup')/shutdown are deprecated in FastAPI - migrate to lifespan context manager.
evaluate() WARN threshold uses hi>0 guard so specs with upper_limit==0 (e.g. no allowed value) will never warn - edge case, acceptable.
save_results silently drops results whose parameter_id is not in the params map (continue) - could hide bad payloads; consider 400.
seed_data_creation: Test workflow created 1 sample REC-2026xxxx-000N under Final Effluent, 1 OOS log entry (rejected then re-approved), 1 dynamic TEST QC user (deactivated by end). Multiple audit entries generated across the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py is a self-contained pytest suite that exercises the whole workflow using Bearer tokens (also validates cookies path via /auth/me). Each run creates one new sample + one new dynamic user - safe to re-run. If brute-force lock is ever tripped by another test, wait 15 min or clear login_attempts collection. Login lockout was intentionally NOT triggered against seeded accounts to keep them usable.
